---
title: "Ingesting lab data"
subtitle: "The main focus of this testing round"
---

The central goal of this pilot is **getting cyanotoxin lab chemistry into FHAB and connected to
the right event / report / case**. Lab results arrive in several shapes — an email folder from
Bend Genetics, a CEDEN export, a one-off spreadsheet for a single site — so there are a few ways
in. This page walks each one, then the **reconciliation** step that links the data to events.

::: {.callout-tip title="Where these live"}
Everything below is under the top-level **Ingest Data** menu (staff only), except attaching
results to a single report/case, which is on the report/case page itself.
:::

## Pick the path that matches how the data arrived

| The lab data arrived as… | Use | Menu |
|---|---|---|
| A **folder of email attachments** from Bend/partner (a results spreadsheet + chain-of-custody / transmittal / receipt PDFs) — **or the raw `.eml` / `.msg` email** | **Ingest lab email folders** | Ingest Data → *Ingest lab email folders* |
| A **CEDEN WaterChemistry CSV** (the Bend→CEDEN workflow output) | **Upload CEDEN lab data** | Ingest Data → *Upload CEDEN lab data* |
| A **full CEDEN chemistry template** where StationCode + date is the only link to an event | **Lab batch reconciliation** | Ingest Data → *Lab batch reconciliation* |
| Results for **one already-known report or case** | **Attach on the report/case** | Reports / Cases → *Lab upload* |

All paths land the samples where you can **reconcile** them (link to events) on the **Lab data
workboard**. Start with the workflow that matches your file; the rest of the page is the same
downstream.

---

## A. Email folder upload (Bend / partner) — the newest path

Labs typically email a **folder**: a wide-format results spreadsheet (analytes across columns)
plus a scanned **chain-of-custody (CoC)**, a **transmittal letter**, and a **sample-receipt
form**. This path converts that spreadsheet, brings the samples in, and **keeps the original
files on the batch** for provenance.

**Steps**

1. **Ingest Data → Ingest lab email folders**.
2. Under *Folder files*, select **all** the files from the one email folder (the results CSV/XLSX
   **and** the PDFs). Add a **Source label** like `Clear Lake (RB5)` (optional but helpful).
3. **Ingest folder.** You'll get a summary — *"Ingested N samples (M geocoded), K results; stored
   J files"* — and land on the workboard filtered to that batch.

::: {.callout-tip title="Drop in the raw email (.eml / .msg)"}
You don't have to pull the attachments out first. You can select the **whole lab email** — a saved
`.eml` or an Outlook `.msg` — and its attachments (the **results spreadsheet** and the
**CoC / transmittal / receipt PDFs**) are unpacked and ingested automatically. Inline signature
logos are skipped; the email **body** and the **original message** are kept on the batch for
provenance; and if you leave *Source label* blank, the email's **subject line** becomes the batch
label. You can mix a `.msg`/`.eml` with loose files in the same selection.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Many folders at once"}
Have a **parent folder that holds many lab folders** (one per email)? Use the **Many folders at
once** box on the same screen: pick the parent folder and **Ingest all subfolders**. Each
subfolder becomes its own batch (labeled with the subfolder name), uploaded one at a time with a
running progress line — so a 50-folder set won't overload a single request. The tally at the end
names any folders that failed so you can retry just those.
:::

**What happens**

- The wide spreadsheet is converted to CEDEN long form: each analyte value becomes a result
  (ELISA toxins, dry-weight toxins, qPCR genes, chlorophyll). `ND` becomes a proper non-detect.
- Samples come in **unlinked** and are **geocoded from the CEDEN station registry** when the
  station code is known. Samples whose station isn't in the registry come in **ungeocoded** —
  their coordinates usually live on the CoC (see [Geocoding](#geocoding-ungeocoded-samples)).
- The **source files stay on the batch**: on the workboard batch banner (and the *Ingested
  batches* table) you'll see `coc · data · receipt · transmittal` links — they open in a **new
  tab** so your workspace stays put.

**What to test**

- Upload a folder; do the sample/result/geocoded counts look right?
- Open the stored **CoC** link — does it open in a new tab and show the scanned form?
- A folder with **no results spreadsheet** (only PDFs) should still store the files.
- Do the samples appear on the **workboard**, filtered to the new batch?

---

## B. Upload CEDEN lab data (workflow output)

For a **CEDEN WaterChemistry CSV** (the output of the Bend→CEDEN workflow), use **Ingest Data →
Upload CEDEN lab data**. You can upload a file or pull from a URL. This loads samples + results,
geocodes stations from the registry, and **auto-links** samples to nearby events where it's
confident.

**What to test:** upload a CEDEN chemistry CSV; confirm samples/results load and that obvious
station+date matches auto-link (the rest wait on the workboard).

---

## C. Lab batch reconciliation (CEDEN template, staged)

For a **full CEDEN chemistry template** where you want to review every link before it's written,
use **Ingest Data → Lab batch reconciliation**.

1. Upload the template CSV. Optionally widen the **match radius (m)** and **± days** window.
2. The batch is **staged** — nothing touches live reports yet.
3. For each **station + date group**, the matcher suggests candidate reports within the windows.
   **Promote** a confident match, **link** manually, or **create a report** from the station.
4. Use **Auto-link** to accept all high-confidence, unambiguous matches at once, then review the
   rest.

**What to test:** stage a template; confirm nothing is linked until you act; try Auto-link, then
link one group manually and create a report from another.

---

## D. Attach results to one report or case

When results belong to a **single known site**, skip matching entirely: open the **report** (or
**case**) and use its **Lab upload** to attach a CEDEN CSV directly. Every sample pins to that
report/case.

---

## After ingest: reconcile on the Lab data workboard

**Ingest Data → Lab data workboard** is where lab samples get connected to events/reports/cases
and quality-reviewed. It's built as a **task board**: the lead **assigns** work, team members
**link**, a reviewer **QA-approves** or **flags**.

- **Status chips:** *Unlinked*, *Linked · awaiting QA*, *Flagged for rework*, *QA approved*, and
  *Routine sampling*, plus **Geocoded · not linked**, **Needs geocoding**, and **📎 Needs geocoding ·
  has files** — click one to filter. The first two split the unlinked pile into samples that are
  ready to research (they have a location) versus those still waiting on coordinates; the last one
  is the **actionable subset** — samples that need coordinates *and* have a CoC on file to read them
  off. Start there. **The counts on the chips reflect the filters you've applied** — set a region or
  a batch and the tallies re-count for just that view, so you can see, e.g., how many samples in
  *this* ingest still need geocoding.
- **Filters:** status, assignee (incl. **Me** / Unassigned), region, a **Geocoding** filter
  (Geocoded / Not geocoded), a **Files** filter (**Has files** / **No files**), and a station /
  water-body search. A batch link filters the board to just that ingest.
- **Each row shows its provenance:** the sampling event, a **📎 file count** (linking to the batch's
  stored files) or *"no files"*, the **ingestion date**, and the **Result ID** — so you can tell at
  a glance which items have a CoC to work from, and cite an exact result when doing QC.
- **Assign:** check rows, pick a team member under *"With checked rows →"*, **Assign**.
- **Per sample:** **Link / Re-link** by report (R#) or case (C#); **+Report** (create one from the
  station); **✓ QA** approve; **⚑** flag with a reason; **Unlink**; **Routine** (see below).
  *Re-linking clears QA so the sample returns to the review queue.*
- **Batch reconcile:** *Reconcile checked* or *Reconcile all unlinked in this view* auto-links the
  confident, unambiguous matches in one pass.

### The results map (🗺 Map of results) — explore & multi-select

Above the table, **Map of results** opens a map of every geocoded sample in the **current filtered
view** (set a region, batch, or status first to focus it). Markers are colored by status
(unlinked, linked, QA-approved, flagged, routine). It's built for exploring links and picking
several samples at once:

- Click a marker to see the sample and jump to its row.
- Use **Select all in view** — or tick individual samples on the map/table — to build a selection,
  then **assign** or act on the whole set together. Filtering first and then multi-selecting the
  filtered results is the quickest way to move a batch of related samples through the same edit.

### The sample map (🗺) — the research popup

Click a sample's **🗺** to open its context map. This is where the tedious research/linking
happens, so it gathers everything in one place:

- A **provenance summary**: how the sample was ingested (*Email folder ingest — <folder>*, *CEDEN
  chemistry upload*, *Lab batch reconciliation*, *data.ca.gov / legacy import*), the **sampling
  event (SE) id, batch kind, ingestion date, and who ingested it**, its lab identity (station, type,
  BG_ID, lab sample id, lab batch, project), result count, and its **source files**
  (`coc · data · transmittal …`, opening in a new tab) — or *"no source files stored for this
  ingest"* when there aren't any. This is where you look when a sample is confusing and you need to
  trace exactly where it came from.
- The **map**: the sample as a **★**, and nearby reports colored by how close in **time** they are
  to the sample (blue ≤14 d, yellow 14–30 d, pink 30–60 d, gray >60 d). Click a marker to link to
  that report or its case, or open the report in a new tab.
- A **list of the nearby reports** below the map (same reports as the markers) — handy when
  markers overlap and are hard to click. Check **one** to link the sample to that report, or check
  **several that share a case** and **Link selected** to link the sample to that case at once.

### Geocoding ungeocoded samples {#geocoding-ungeocoded-samples}

Samples whose station isn't in the registry come in **without a location** — their coordinates
are usually on the **CoC**. Use the **📎 Needs geocoding · has files** chip to jump straight to the
ones you can act on.

::: {.callout-note title="Needs geocoding but has no files — what happened?"}
Attached files live on a sample's **ingest batch**, and only some paths bring them in: the
**folder / email** path stores the CoC, transmittal, and receipt; the **prepared-CSV import** and
**CEDEN uploads** bring **no PDFs**. So an item that needs geocoding *and* has no files came in one
of those ways — its CoC is still in the **original lab email**, not in the system. To fix it, find
that email and **re-ingest it as a folder / `.eml` / `.msg`** — that attaches the CoC (and can OCR
coordinates off it), turning a no-file item into a workable one. The row's **ingestion date** and
**SE** in the provenance summary help you find the original.
:::

On the sample map you can:

1. Open the batch's **CoC** (new tab) and read the latitude/longitude.
2. Type them into the **lat / long** boxes → **Search nearby** to preview reports/cases around
   that point (shown as a ◆).
3. **Save to sample** to store the coordinates — the sample is now geocoded, appears on the main
   map, and becomes eligible for batch reconcile.
4. **Scan CoC (OCR)** will try to read the coordinates off the CoC automatically. *In the current
   hosted pilot this is a best-effort helper and may report that OCR isn't available* — if so,
   just read the CoC and type the numbers.

There are also two batch-level ways to enter coordinates:

- **Per-sample entry screen** — when a batch has several samples that each have their **own**
  coordinates on the CoC (often under IDs different from the lab's sample IDs). From the *Ingested
  batches* table (**Enter coords**) or the workboard batch banner (**Enter sample coordinates**),
  open a screen that lists every sample in the batch — station, **customer / CoC label**, **lab
  sample id**, BG_ID, date, type — with a latitude/longitude box each, and the CoC linked at top.
  Transcribe each sample's coordinates and **Save**. Each sample gets its **own** point, so samples
  the ingest put on one station are split apart correctly.
- **Bulk paste** — **Ingest Data → Bulk sample coordinates**: paste one row per line as
  `station code, latitude, longitude` (codes with spaces/commas are fine — the last two numbers are
  taken as lat/long). Matching a station geocodes every sample at it.

### Routine sampling (not every sample is a bloom report)

Some samples are **routine monitoring**, not tied to any bloom report or case. On an unlinked
sample, use **Routine** (row button or the map popup's *Tag routine sampling*) to move it into the
**Routine sampling** bucket so it stops showing as unfinished work. **↩ Unlinked** puts it back.
*(Routine sub-types will come later.)*

---

## Managing lab data: the ingestion report, cleanup & duplicates

Once data is in, three tools under **Ingest Data** help you audit it, remove junk, and fix
double-ups. All three are staff-only.

### Ingestion report — what came in, and how well {#ingestion-report}

**Ingest Data → Ingestion report** is a filterable audit of **every ingestion**. Four tiles at the
top summarize the current view — **Ingestions, Samples, Geocoded %, Results**. Filter by **kind**
(email/folder vs. reconciliation), **region**, **ingested-from / to** dates, or a **search** on
source or SE ID; **Download CSV** exports the filtered rows.

Rows are **grouped by upload session** — a multi-folder upload (or one prepared CSV) is a single
ingestion, so a 50-folder drop shows as one session you can expand to its individual folders. Each
session shows **who ran it and when**, how many folders, the sample/geocoded/result/file totals,
its **geocoded-% health pill**, and the **lab-result date range** it covers.

::: {.callout-warning title="Deleting whole ingestions"}
Made a bad drop, or ingested a test folder you want gone? Tick a session's **select** box (it
selects every folder in it) — or tick individual folders, across sessions — then use the sticky
**🗑 Delete selected ingestions** bar and type **DELETE** to confirm. This removes each selected
folder **and everything it brought in**: its samples, their results, and the stored source files.
It's **audited** and **cannot be undone**. A folder whose samples have already been **linked to a
report/case** is *kept* and named in a notice, so you don't drop case data by accident — tick
**delete even when linked** only if you really mean to.
:::

### Clean up empty records — near-empty ingestion artifacts {#cleanup}

Malformed rows sometimes land as **near-empty samples** — no measurement value, text, or qualifier.
**Ingest Data → Clean up empty records** finds them so you can remove them safely.

- **Triage modes** split *totally blank* rows (no station/date/id at all) from ones that carry a
  **station/date/id but no data** — clean out the pure blanks first.
- Filter by **ingest batch (SE)** or a **station/BG_ID/source** search. You can also **search by
  analyte name** — the page lists **every analyte present on the empty rows** (with counts) as
  quick filters, so you can see exactly what the artifacts are.
- Tick the bad rows and **Delete**. The delete is **guarded**: it only ever removes rows that are
  genuinely empty **and** unlinked (anything else in your selection is skipped), and every deletion
  is **audited**.

### Find & fix duplicate records {#duplicates}

The same physical sample can arrive twice (folder ingest *and* a data.ca.gov pull, say).
**Ingest Data → Find duplicate samples** now opens as a **report** and lets you resolve them.

- **Summary tiles:** duplicate **sample groups** and **redundant sample records**, plus possible
  duplicate **reports** and redundant report records. Filter by **sampling event** or a
  station/BG_ID/lab-ID/source search.
- **Each group shows *why* it matched** — an explicit lab sample id, sample id, or BG_ID, or the
  weaker *station + date + type* (flagged **⚠️ composite key**, since that can be a legitimate field
  replicate) — plus the fingerprint. For each group you can either:
  - **Merge** the duplicates into the one you mark **Keep** (results and links are repointed onto
    the survivor and its results de-duplicated), or
  - tick the redundant copies for a **batch delete** (type **DELETE**; linked rows are skipped;
    audited).
- A read-only **Possible duplicate reports** section groups reports that share a water body, date,
  and region — open each to decide which to keep (report de-duplication stays manual, since cases
  and advisories hang off those IDs).

### Deleting a single sample {#delete-sample}

To remove **one** sample, open it in the **Sample work area** (Ingest Data → *Sample work area* →
click a sample) and use the **Delete this sample** box at the bottom: type **DELETE** to confirm.
It removes the sample and its results, is **audited**, and — like the tools above — is **blocked if
the sample is linked to a report/case** unless you tick **delete even though linked**.

---

## Suggested lab-ingest test script (~15 min)

1. **Ingest an email folder** (Ingest Data → *Ingest lab email folders*) — pick all files from one
   lab folder, add a source label, ingest. Check the counts and open the stored **CoC** (new tab).
   *(Or try **Many folders at once** with a parent folder of several subfolders.)*
2. On the **workboard**, use the **Geocoded · not linked** chip; open a sample's **🗺** and read its
   **provenance summary** (how it was ingested + files), then **link** it to a nearby report from
   the list — or **+Report** to create one.
3. Use the **Needs geocoding** chip to find an **ungeocoded** sample; read its coordinates off the
   CoC, type them in, **Search nearby**, then **Save to sample**. For a batch with several samples,
   try the batch's **Enter coords** screen instead.
4. Tag one sample as **Routine sampling**, then confirm it appears under the *Routine* chip.
5. Run **Reconcile all unlinked in this view** and see how many auto-link.
6. Open **Lab** (results browser) and confirm your batch's results appear; **Download CSV**.
7. Open the **[Ingestion report](#ingestion-report)** — find your upload session, check the who/when
   and geocoded-% look right. *(Optional, on a throwaway test drop: select it and try **🗑 Delete
   selected ingestions** to confirm it clears the samples/results/files.)*
8. Note anything confusing along the way — see [Giving feedback](feedback.qmd).
